messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT — Network egress anomalies detected in SFO (03:42 UTC). Elevated packet loss + intermittent BGP withdraws observed to TransitOne. Auto-paging #incidents and on-call network.
alexg: I'm oncall (alexg). seeing >2% packet loss from sfo-edge1 -> TransitOne. BGP shows repeated withdraw/announce cycles for a subset of our SFO prefixes.
maria-net: taking network lead. pulling bgp summary and checking control-plane CPU/queues.
kevin-sre: I'm watching infra + synthetic checks. p95 latency spiking for SFO edge and API error rate rising ~5% for SFO-origin traffic.
maria-net: route snapshot from sfo-edge1:

```
show ip bgp summary
Neighbor        AS      Up/Down    Prefixes   State
203.0.113.1    64512   00:02      4123/4123   flapping/est
```

maria-net: Also seeing DNS path divergence — authoritative in SFO returning different A records intermittently; some recursive resolvers hitting alternate transit and timing out after TTL expiry.
alexg: hypothesis: TransitOne has a partial blackholing or instability causing our routes to be intermittently withdrawn. This leads to DNS recursion sometimes failing -> clients get stale IPs or no responses.
kevin-sre: impact summary: client requests to SFO region -> 502/timeouts. ~5% of global requests affected, concentrated in SFO. No detected data corruption.
maria-net: mitigation plan: 1) announce less-specific escape aggregate to TransitTwo (AS64496), 2) shorten DNS TTLs for SFO auth while we validate, 3) open TAC with TransitOne.
alexg: proceeding with BGP change. @oncall-net ok to proceed?
oncall-net: confirmed, proceed. Kevin, prep traffic-shift playbook and status page blurb.
maria-net: announcing /18 aggregate to AS64496 now.

```
! router sfo-edge1
router bgp 65100
 neighbor 198.51.100.2 remote-as 64496
 network 198.51.240.0/18 route-map SFO-ESCAPE out
!
route-map SFO-ESCAPE permit 10
 set local-preference 200
```

maria-net: Advertisement sent. monitoring BGP convergence...
alexg: TransitTwo picked it up. BGP session stable on sfo-edge1 and flaps subsided.
kevin-sre: synthetic checks: p95 latency returning to baseline; API error rates trending down. Est. customer impact window: 03:42–03:58 UTC (~16 minutes).
maria-net: opened TAC ticket with TransitOne: INC-8427. They acknowledge partial capacity disruption. Asking for community tags — sending route-map details and asking for any filtering info.
alexg: updating DNS TTLs now: set to 30s for SFO authoritative zone while we validate. Will revert after 1h of healthy metrics.
kevin-sre: drafting status page update. @ops-comm can you publish once I give final wording?
ops-comm: got it — will publish with mitigation notes and ETA once you send the final.
maria-net: enabling extra telemetry: netflow sampling and tcpdump on sfo-edge1 for suspect prefixes to capture packet-level behavior.
oncall-net: handing off to night shift @jess-network at 04:15 UTC. If BGP withdraws resume >3x in 5m escalate to L3.
jess-network: ack, taking handoff. Will run DDoS checks and keep watch on TransitOne/TW sessions.
kevin-sre: post-incident actions (prelim): 1) correlate TransitOne logs and our tcpdumps, 2) evaluate permanent routing policy to prefer multipath + community-based escape, 3) add automated detection for DNS path divergence.
maria-net: follow-up: add synthetic DNS queries from multiple regions to detect divergence earlier and ensure resolvers respect TTL changes.
alexg: closing criteria: metrics stable for 30m and night shift ack. Current plan to monitor; if no regressions we'll close and start postmortem.
incident-bot: STATUS UPDATE — mitigated. Traffic rerouted via TransitTwo, TransitOne TAC engaged. PagerDuty incident PD-39821 created. Postmortem scheduled. :white_check_mark:
